expectation: StationAI opens one main board window titled with its worktree label and the bridge reports API version 1.

The primary and linked source worktrees resolve to stable, distinct app and XPC identities, build paths, data stores, logs, and managed worktree roots; a saved conversation remains visible after an app restart.

New Task immediately opens an empty conversation with the repository picker focused and a visible red missing-working-folder warning; sending stays disabled until a working folder is added. A persisted empty-root task shows the same red warning when its conversation is reopened. The CLI accepts empty-root tasks and rejects blank titles, missing folders, unavailable roots, and invalid merge targets.

A directly created conversation can add repositories in order, edit pending branch settings, and add a context folder; these settings persist across fresh connections without creating branches or worktrees before the first send. Saving an unsent prompt records task creation, prompt save, and subsequent reads with safe argument metadata, result state, and outcome while excluding prompt text.
A selected existing branch remains pending until task start, then reuses its exact existing worktree path.

The conversation picker can add multiple repositories; unset branch settings display defaults and persist pending auto records resolved to local main without creating branches or worktrees before the first send.
A folder-only task persists its context without Git worktrees and reaches Done after a successful turn without attempting a merge.
Adding a repository branch already assigned to another active task is rejected in the new conversation, and the existing task and repository reservation remain unchanged.
Two concurrent CLI/XPC creates targeting the same explicit branch in one repository serialize through a shared cross-process lock, leaving exactly one persisted active task and rejecting the other.

If another process holds the shared task-store write lock when a Codex turn completes after an explicit completed outcome, final status persistence waits and then saves Review status and full history across fresh CLI/XPC reads. Correlated persistence diagnostics include task ID, store path, lock wait, attempts, and retry count; task reads correlate started and completed events by read ID and store path, while failed reads include store file and sidecar state. Reopening the conversation in the UI shows the saved exchange without a store error.

A real ModelContainer open failure against an isolated invalid store path returns an error and durably logs the phase, exact underlying NSError domain/code/userInfo, resolved store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and read-only schema probe failure; the paired visible UI case keeps StationAI open on its normal board while the same isolated CLI/XPC request fails and verifies the persisted diagnostic.

A real SwiftData fetch failure against an isolated store with a missing task column returns an error and logs a correlated read ID, NSError domain/code/userInfo, store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and the exact missing-column message from a read-only schema probe before the CLI/XPC request completes; the paired visible UI case keeps the normal task board open and verifies the same isolated failure record.

A real legacy SwiftData task store with old model metadata and no submitted-prompt column waits for the store-write lock while CLI/XPC reads concurrently; migration backs up before repair, and the CLI preserves the task and draft. The visible app then opens against the migrated store and preserves the draft through a subsequent restart; metadata advances and later opens create no additional backup. The store is imported once into the protected filename and the legacy database remains unchanged. Committed WAL-only draft data survives import, and a subsequent edited draft survives restart without reimport.

A test-built StationAI service rejects a data directory outside the temporary test area and a linked store inside it before creating or opening either store; the visible app remains on its isolated board and can still read its tasks.

Tasks with the same automatic branch choice remain pending without creating a worktree before conversation start; the opt-in live Codex integration sends both turns concurrently and confirms only one task claims the generated branch.

Sending the first message derives an auto branch from the generated task title. Every linked PR must be merged before the task can move to Done. App focus checks each linked PR; an unmerged PR keeps its link and suppresses the completion button. After all PRs merge, focus replaces their links with a green completion button, whose click waits for the task lock, rechecks merge state, and moves the task to Done. Completion preserves the source branch and worktree without merging into the local target, retains conversation history, and exposes the task in the searchable read-only archive.
Moving a reviewed task to Done changes only task status and preserves dirty worktree files, branch, and target commit without committing or merging.
The one-time lifecycle rollout clears task records and clean managed worktrees, preserves branches, and retains dirty managed worktrees with a notice.

With both pairs populated, the board keeps Blocked above Backlog and Waiting Response above In Progress, allows vertical scrolling to reach lower backlog tasks, leaves Review as its own column, hides empty status sections, removes Done from the columns, and rejects manual changes to Codex-owned task status; ⌘F reveals and focuses a prominent board search that filters task cards by title as text changes, while close restores all cards. Answering a question without an explicit completed outcome leaves the task in Waiting Response. Task card titles use slightly expanded letter spacing and line spacing.

The CLI publishes standard and custom progress only during an active task turn, persists each report across fresh CLI/XPC connections, rejects invalid reports, and clears explicitly. During an active turn the CLI accepts completed and waiting-response outcomes, rejects invalid or inactive outcomes, and persists the selected status; without an outcome call, a successful turn ends in Waiting Response. The board shows progress details and places completed tasks in Review and waiting or omitted outcomes in Waiting Response. New threads receive hidden progress and outcome instructions at thread start, and existing threads receive them on resume; turn requests do not repeat the instructions. Only an explicit completed outcome reaches Review.

Progress reports clear when turns fail or are interrupted and when Codex requests user input; a staged completed outcome is discarded if its turn fails, leaving the task Blocked. The task card removes the report while lifecycle states remain Blocked or Waiting Response, and answering the question resumes the task successfully.
A rename waits for the real per-task operation lock, then persists across fresh CLI/XPC reads; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.

Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, rejects an empty list, and waits for an active conversation turn; a stale Git-folder validation is rejected after a newer folder edit, and the newer roots remain saved.

Repository suggestions can be filtered and navigated with Up/Down, and Enter selects the highlighted repository; adding it waits for an active conversation turn, then persists a pending auto branch with labeled branch, merge-from, and merge-to values, and no worktree exists before the first send.

Pending repository branch, merge-from, and merge-to settings wait for an active conversation turn, then persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads; invalid settings leave prior values intact, and settings are locked after worktree creation.
If a pending repository is removed while its settings are being validated, the stale edit is rejected and the newer repository removal and context root remain saved.

Removing the only pending repository leaves the task with no workspace and preserves the source repository; removing a pending repository preserves other context folders; removing a clean managed worktree waits for an active conversation turn and then succeeds, while a dirty worktree rejects removal and preserves its task record and files.

The task context menu offers deletion. Pending repository tasks delete without confirmation and preserve the source repository; confirmed deletion waits for an active conversation turn; clean started worktrees can be deleted; dirty started worktrees require confirmation, and canceling preserves the task and worktree. CLI delete-check derives and reports the confirmation requirement from saved task and worktree state without resuming the Codex thread; confirmed deletion removes the managed worktree.

A real worktree-removal failure records the task title and task, thread, process, phase, and underlying error details, including bounded NSError user-info keys and values, without recording conversation text; the failed task and worktree remain available and deletion succeeds after the repository is restored.

The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected; a fresh CLI read and repository discovery use the persisted parent. Dark and Light appearance choices persist, and the ask-each-time, resolve-and-push, resolve-only, and keep-PR conflict preferences validate and persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads and are editable in Settings; appearance changes update the open Settings picker.

The CLI returns top-level Git repository suggestions while excluding nested repositories and symlink targets. The conversation picker shows those suggestions, filters by repository name or parent path, and reports no matches for non-repository folders.

The CLI reads and writes ordered last-selected repositories across fresh XPC connections and applies them to empty tasks through repository batches with ordered roots and default auto/main/main branch settings; a newly saved list applies to a fresh task and remains saved. Invalid repository paths are rejected without changing the saved preference. In the UI, the picker placeholder shows saved repository names in order followed immediately by a Return key indicator; blank Return restores the saved repositories, while typing and arrow selection replaces and persists the list for the next conversation.

Applying an ordered repository batch with a valid repository followed by an empty Git repository fails without mutation: the CLI reports invalid_argument and fresh reads show no repository attachments or workspace roots; New Task blank Return keeps the picker open, shows an error, attaches neither repository, keeps roots empty, and preserves the saved repository order.
Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task.

The CLI creates an Untitled task with no roots, logs task.create.succeeded for its ID, verifies empty history, and deletes it cleanly. New Task logs start and completion events with the same attempt ID and created task ID, then opens one empty conversation with its repository picker focused and no create sheet. Adding folder-only context leaves history empty, and backing out deletes the pending task without confirmation.

A real directory at the task-store write-lock path makes CLI task creation fail with operation_failed and leaves no task persisted; the paired New Task button shows the save error and writes correlated start and failure diagnostics with the same attempt ID, error domain, and code.

Creating a repository task leaves its selected branch pending while the composer automatically saves an unsent prompt as it is typed; clearing the composer clears the stored draft, backing out needs no Save button, and reopening restores the draft without creating a branch or worktree. Blank drafts cannot be stored, and invalid status changes are rejected without mutation. If the title is renamed while delayed title generation is in flight, the late result is skipped, the renamed title persists, and diagnostics record the skip reason without prompt or title text.

Shift+Enter inserts a newline at the caret without sending and Return submits; multiline prompts persist as typed text, the composer expands beyond five lines, stops at its 12-line limit, and retains all lines while scrolling. Long saved drafts reopen intact and immediately expand before typing, including after restart, remain editable, grow for wrapped text, shrink when shortened, and show their own overflow scrollbar for earlier and later content. The CLI/XPC preserves a 15-line draft. Long submitted prompts persist through CLI/XPC, and the UI transcript shows a scrollbar for overflow with scrolling that reveals earlier and later content. Blank drafts cannot be sent or stored, sent prompts persist in conversation history through reload, and backing out immediately after send preserves the submitted prompt as a sent message while title generation is pending. The CLI rejects submitted-prompt saves unless they include nonblank text and In Progress status. The CLI/XPC and UI also recover a submitted prompt that has no Codex thread or active send reservation: the task becomes Blocked, the pending marker clears, and the prompt returns to the composer. Sending to an Untitled auto-branch task derives its branch from the Codex-generated title or from the prompt fallback when title generation fails. During title preparation, CLI/XPC confirms the submitted prompt and conversation thread remain attached to the task, while the UI keeps Pause disabled until the task's conversation client has an interruptible turn. Persistent diagnostics correlate title generation and application outcomes with the task and Codex thread, record failure or skip reasons, and exclude prompt and title text, including text echoed in server errors. Queued follow-ups persist with task and thread identity across fresh CLI/XPC reads, dispatch once after the next completed turn, and disappear from the queue after completion. During an active turn, the UI exposes separate steer and queue actions, sends steering with the active turn ID, and retains the queued follow-up across reopening.

Two concurrent sends for the same task are serialized across the app and CLI/XPC paths against the local Codex app-server fixture; the second waits for the first, both complete on the persisted thread, the task remains In Progress while a send is active, and successful turns without outcome calls finish in Waiting Response.

While a Codex turn is active, a stale steer response is shown as an error and preserves the draft for retry; malformed steer images fail validation; CLI/XPC steering routes image data through the mailbox to a UI-owned active turn and appears in the visible conversation; an accepted UI Steer action sends attached image data with text using the matching active turn ID, displays it in the transcript, and clears its draft and image preview. The user can also persist a distinct follow-up for after completion; it dispatches once after a matching completed notification, survives fresh CLI/XPC reads, and is removed only after successful delivery.

The conversation composer accepts images from the picker and paste, previews them before sending, compresses large clipboard images to fit the 10 MB payload limit, sends PNG and JPEG data URLs through CLI/XPC and to Codex using the tagged image URL payload, reads Codex history image URLs, and keeps earlier images visible after a later text turn and history refresh. Diagnostics record image MIME and encoded size without storing image payloads.
Malformed image data is rejected with a visible composer error and an invalid_argument bridge response, without creating conversation history or advancing task status.

During a parent turn, started and interacted updates coalesce by child thread ID into clear named timeline rows outside the collapsible Codex activity section, with sentence-style names, available path/model/reasoning metadata, and started-working wording; completed and interrupted states, optional metadata, and unknown kinds survive history reload and remain visible after reopening the task conversation. The child thread opens as read-only through thread/read, thread/turns/list, and thread/items/list without editable controls or thread/resume, and diagnostics retain safe RPC outcomes while excluding conversation text, command output, and diffs.

Selecting Plan mode sends a planning turn; a completed <proposed_plan> is automatically rendered as Markdown with visible spacing between distinct paragraphs and without exposing its wrapper tags, including after reopening, while bridge history preserves the exact source and the reopened conversation shows its latest message.
The composer shows a Codex-reported model, while unsupported modes and malformed model IDs are rejected before creating history.

Structured questions raised in Plan mode move the task into the conditional Waiting Response board section even when Codex marks the request non-blocking; reopening preserves its status, keyed answers resume In Progress, and the answered turn returns to Waiting Response without an explicit completed outcome.
Non-blocking structured questions remain visible without moving the task out of In Progress, then the answered turn returns to Waiting Response without an explicit completed outcome.

Turn start persists In Progress; reopening while a turn is still active recovers the stale task to Blocked with a reason. Interrupted outcomes persist Blocked across connections, and diagnostics identify the failed turn phase and store path; a new prompt can finish in Review. A queued follow-up remains visible as needing action after interruption, survives reopening, and is dispatched only after an explicit retry; the completed retry becomes the task's latest saved prompt.

A failed turn preserves its blocked reason and appears in the compact Blocked section above Backlog with a user-intervention indication; retrying clears that section, and the successful retry returns to Waiting Response without an explicit completed outcome.

The task view separates staged and working Git changes, and selecting text or JSON files opens a calculated, highlighted side-by-side diff over the conversation. Diagnostics record inventory and file-read outcomes with paths and byte counts, without logging file contents.
External file edits and Git commits update the open task's changes sidebar automatically, and fresh CLI connections report the same Git status.

The CLI confirms a new repository-backed task persists in Backlog; the UI shows no PR control there, then shows the active-card PR action after the conversation completes. The Done archive control retains its help and waits for the task lock before publication failure without saving a PR link or changing Done status.

The real Git CLI detects conflicts without mutation, requires confirmation by default, honors saved keep without publishing, resolves staged conflicts locally without pushing, and commits and pushes a staged resolution without changing the target; unknown actions are rejected. The paired UI verifies unresolved conflicts stay uncommitted and unpublished, presents keep, resolve-only, and resolve-and-push with the remember checkbox, verifies remembered choices skip confirmation and persist in Settings, and confirms resolve-only commits staged resolution locally while the remote task branch remains absent.

A Done task's real SwiftData record retains a linked PR number and URL across fresh CLI/XPC reads so the archive renders the PR link with distinct hover emphasis and useful help; an active repository-backed task card renders a saved PR link with the same hover indication.

Explicit app overrides reject obsolete compatibility metadata, foreign worktree or bridge identities, test IDs that do not match the current worktree, and nonisolated test data before launching; the current app preserves a saved draft across restart.
An invalid legacy database fails import without changing the source or publishing a destination or partial snapshot; the normal isolated board remains usable.
